decisions.statement: A process is a stray where the transcript records its subagent returned.
A process is a stray where the index carries no page for its subagent's seat.
Whether the seat has a page is read before the transcript is.
An index that would not answer leaves the subagent unread rather than gone.
A process whose subagent the transcript names as working is no stray.
A process whose subagent the transcript could not be read for is no stray.
A reading says which subagents it could not tell about.
A process stating an acting agent that names no subagent is passed over.
The environment a process was started with does not carry a name exported inside that process.
A shell a tool call runs in is therefore named by its command line rather than by its environment.
The command line is read only in the shape the harness composes.
A command line that merely mentions an acting agent names none.
The environment is taken where the two disagree.
No page's body is read to tell whether a subagent has returned.
An index read as carrying no page where it would not answer would make every seat look gone.
How long a process has run is not read here.
Nothing here signals or ends a process.
A subagent's page goes only once what that subagent left running has stopped.
A page that outlives its subagent that way says nothing, so no page is read here.

definition: a process still running under a subagent that has departed
